newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia 1997 oil exports via Ukrain seen at 16 mln.
newsitem.headline: Russia 1997 oil exports via Ukrain seen at 16 mln.

text.p: Russian oil supplies to Central and Eastern Europe in 1997 through the Ukrainian stretch of the Druzhba pipeline will be flat at around 16.0 million tonnes, a senior oil official said on Thursday.
Stepan Yaloveha, spokesman for the State Oil and Gas Committee, said talks with Russian oil exporters on contracts were continuing but that supplies would not tail off sharply.

"There will be both inter-state and commercial contracts, but the annual amount of transported oil will be at least 16.0 million tonnes, despite the fact that we could transport up to 20.0 million tonnes," Yaloveha told Reuters by telephone.
Flows via Ukraine's stretch of the Druzhba (Friendship in Russian) pipeline fell to 16.6 million tonnes in 1996 from 18.0 million tonnes in 1995.
About 80 Russian energy firms supply oil via Druzhba to the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and former Yugoslavia.

Druzhba's total capacity, including the Belarussian stretch to Poland and Germany, is about 60 million tonnes. But the link has been under-utilised since the 1991 collapse of the former Soviet Union, when many European clients diversified oil supplies or had no cash to pay.
Yaloveha said Druzhba has been charging Russian suppliers $5.20 per tonne of oil transported across the whole Ukrainian stretch of the link.
